## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Oguṇṭhita Sikkhāpada* (Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 67) is a training rule from the Vinaya Piṭaka regulating monastic etiquette and conduct during the transmission of the Dhamma [SuttaCentral]. The rule establishes that a Buddhist monastic must not preach the Dhamma to anyone whose head is covered (*oguṇṭhita*), unless that individual is ill; teaching someone under such circumstances is prohibited because listening with the head covered constitutes a sign of disrespect toward the Dhamma [Bodhi 2003]. Modern English translations of the text include that by Bhikkhu Brahmali hosted on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral]. In secondary scholarship on the Suttas, the rule is noted by Bhikkhu Bodhi as part of a recurring set of Vinaya decorum rules that forbid preaching to auditors exhibiting disrespectful posture or dress [Bodhi 2003].
The rule is widely attested across early Buddhist Vinaya traditions. Curated parallels recorded by SuttaCentral include the Pali Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Pātimokkhas, the Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Parivāra, and the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (*pli-tv-bi-vb-sk67*), along with corresponding *sekhiya* regulations in the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Dharmaguptaka, Mahāsāṅghika, and Kāśyapīya traditions preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan recensions [SuttaCentral]. Within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus records 105 internal matches across 44 texts, showing that the formulaic phrasing of this training rule shares its highest density of textual overlap with adjacent *sekhiya* rules concerning deportment while teaching the Dhamma, most prominently Sekhiya 66, Sekhiya 72, Sekhiya 71, Sekhiya 62, and Sekhiya 61 [DharmaNexus].
